mathgap.title: Direct count assignment
mathgap.principle: When a statement explicitly gives a numeric count for a person (e.g., "X has N items"), set that person's current count to N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence contains a direct count phrase with a specific number.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as a hint rather than assigning the variable, leaving the count undefined.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer than Y" as X = Y - N, preserving the order of X and Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence contains a comparative phrase with "more" or "fewer" and a numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Swapping X and Y, interpreting "X has N more than Y" as Y = X + N.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives N items to Y", subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count, updating both parties in the order the statement appears.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence describes a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Leaving the receiver's count unchanged after a transfer, resulting in loss of items.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the exact order they appear; later statements must use the counts after all earlier statements have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving a problem with multiple statements that affect counts.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a later comparison using initial counts instead of the updated counts after earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a conditional transfer, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; if the condition holds, apply the transfer, otherwise skip it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement includes a conditional clause like "if X has at least N, then X gives N to Y".
mathgap.example: Applying a conditional transfer without checking the condition, leading to impossible negative counts.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Identify which equations and variables directly or indirectly affect the queried person, and focus on solving those while ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many statements, many of which do not involve the target variable.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system including irrelevant variables, causing unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality parsing
mathgap.principle: Parse statements of the form "The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have" as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a sentence that equates two differences.
mathgap.example: Treating the equality as absolute differences, swapping the order of terms, or ignoring the sign.

mathgap.title: Solve signed difference equations with unknowns
mathgap.principle: When a signed‑difference equality contains unknown variables, rearrange it into a standard linear equation and solve for the unknowns using substitution or elimination.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing a signed difference equality that involves variables not yet known.
mathgap.example: Leaving the equation unsolved or solving it as if it were a simple equality without considering the sign.

mathgap.title: Equal redistribution and splitting handling
mathgap.principle: For statements that redistribute items equally between two persons, set both persons' counts to the average of their combined total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence says two people redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount.
mathgap.example: Assigning each person the sum instead of the average, doubling the total.

mathgap.title: Implicit zero initialization for unknown persons in transfers
mathgap.principle: If a transfer involves a giver or receiver whose count has not been explicitly set or constrained by any prior equation, assume they start with zero before applying the transfer; this allows updating the other party's count correctly while keeping the unknown person's count as a variable if later constrained.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a transfer and one of the participants has no known count at that point.
mathgap.example: Leaving the receiver's count unchanged because the giver's unknown count was not initialized, leading to an unsolvable system.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to interpreting "difference" as a non‑signed distance and may reorder the names, losing the intended sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Parse the statement as (A - B) = (C - D) preserving the order of names on each side; keep the sign.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats all transfers as simultaneous, forgetting that earlier transfers affect later counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply transfers strictly in the order they appear, updating counts after each statement.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats "X has N" as a permanent value, not as a starting point that can change via later transfers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as initial values; allow them to be modified by subsequent transfer statements.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may apply the transfer unconditionally, overlooking the condition that may prevent it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate the condition using the current counts before applying the transfer; skip if false.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting multiplicative increase statements as additive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads "increase by N times" as "add N" instead of multiplying.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize multiplicative language and apply the appropriate scaling (e.g., X = X * (1 + N) or X = X * N).
